 Medline Bed Recall Reported Deaths Rise to 7, With 35 Serious Injuries, as Caregivers Await Repairs
 Published Nov 16, 2026 9:02 AM EST 
 By
 Joseph James 
 Editorial Illustration via AI 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 Medline has now received reports of seven deaths and 35 serious injuries tied to fire and entrapment hazards in its recalled beds, rails, mattresses and accessories, according to a company update the FDA posted on its recalls page Nov. 13. The counts are current as of Nov. 8.
 Reported deaths have more than tripled since the FDA's Oct. 29 early alert, which cited two deaths and 16 serious injuries as of Oct. 20, and reported serious injuries have more than doubled. The update does not say where the deaths occurred, whether they involved fire or entrapment, or whether the added reports reflect new incidents or older ones newly reported to the company.
 For families with a relative in a nursing home or a home-care bed, the higher count turns a recall notice into a to-do list. Confirm the brand, follow the interim safety rules every day, and find out whether the bed qualifies for repair, replacement or a refund.
 Developing Story Note: This report covers new developments involving the recall of all Medline Brand beds and accessories. Information may change as Medline and the FDA release additional findings. Latest verified update: Medline announcement posted by the FDA Nov. 13, 2026, with death and injury reports through Nov. 8, 2026. 
 Seven Deaths and Many Open Questions
 Medline began recalling all Medline Brand beds and associated rails, mattresses and accessories, including hand-control pendants and motor boxes, on Oct. 14 and is discontinuing the beds and exiting the market. The company cites a "potential fire hazard and entrapment risk, which may result in patient injury or death." 
 The products were distributed in the U.S. and Canada from 2011 to 2026 to durable medical equipment providers, long-term care facilities and patients directly. The posting does not say how many beds remain in use. It directs owners to Medline's bed recall page for visual guides, product codes, and labeling instructions.
 MedicalDaily previously reported on the FDA's early alert citing two deaths . Since that report, five more deaths and 19 more serious injuries have been reported to Medline, and the company has detailed a repair-and-replacement program.
 The two hazards work differently. Electrical parts may overheat when a bed is overloaded, a part or motor jams, a pendant is damaged or exposed to fluid, an extension cord is used, or non-Medline pendants or accessories are attached. Overheating can lead to smoke, sparks, melting, or fire . Entrapment risk rises when rails are loose or wobbly , when the bed is used with other accessories or when a user lies on the hand pendant, and entrapment can lead to suffocation.
 The warnings began well before this fall. In February, Medline updated instructions for its homecare beds after reports of hand pendants "sparking, burning, melting, smoking and catching on fire," with 12 injuries and one death tied to the electrical problem as of Dec. 18, 2025, MedTech Dive reported . An FDA recall record for homecare bed pendants shows that action began with customer notices in November 2025 and was expanded in August with more product codes. The FDA classified it as Class I , its most serious category.
 Repair, Replacement or Refund Decisions for Families
 Medline says some beds can be repaired through a Medline-authorized process. If a bed or accessory cannot be repaired, it may be eligible for replacement or a full or partial refund. Those remedies may apply to certain items bought in the past five years. The posting does not say what applies to older beds.
 The first call for most families is not to Medline. The FDA posting tells owners to contact the provider or distributor that supplied the bed, which for many households is a medical equipment company that delivered it under a rental or insurance arrangement. People who bought directly from Medline can call Medline Recall Customer Service at 1-800-950-0128, option 7, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Central Time on weekdays, or email recalls@medline.com.
 Medline says it will soon send new repair-and-replace customer guides to patients and users. Families should not attempt repairs or changes themselves unless Medline authorizes them. Replacement may also take time, so households may need a backup plan for safe sleep and transfers in the meantime.
 Relatives of nursing home residents can ask the facility three direct questions. Are any residents using Medline beds? Are staff unplugging them between adjustments? When will they be repaired or replaced?
 Residents Who Cannot Move Quickly Face the Greatest Danger
 The people most exposed spend long hours in bed, and many cannot react to smoke or free themselves from a gap. That includes older adults, people with dementia or paralysis and patients recovering from surgery. Home caregivers carry particular pressure because there is no overnight staff checking equipment.
 Until a bed is repaired or replaced, the interim instructions are simple. Unplug the bed, plug it in only to reposition the patient, then unplug it again. Do not use an extension cord, and have a second person help with bed movement whenever possible.
 A hot pendant, jammed motors or controls that stop working are signs to unplug the bed and call for service. Any smoke or fire is an emergency: get the person out and call 911. Injuries and malfunctions can be reported to Medline and to the FDA's MedWatch reporting program .
 Neither Medline nor the FDA has said how many beds are in homes compared with facilities, which models were involved in the deaths, or how quickly repairs are being completed.
 The next steps to watch are Medline's customer guides, any FDA classification of the October action, and whether the death count rises again. MedicalDaily will report updates as the FDA posts them.
 Developing Story Timeline
 Nov. 13, 2026: The FDA posts Medline's update reporting seven deaths and 35 serious injuries as of Nov. 8.
 Oct. 29, 2026: The FDA issues an early alert citing two deaths and 16 serious injuries as of Oct. 20.
 Oct. 24, 2026: Medline issues continued-use instructions and repair, replacement and refund options.
 Oct. 14, 2026: Medline begins the recall and announces its exit from the bed market.
 Related MedicalDaily.com Coverage
 Medline Beds Linked to 2 Deaths and 16 Serious Injuries Draw FDA Fire and Entrapment Alert for Caregivers
 Key Questions Answered
 How many deaths are linked to the Medline bed recall? Medline has received reports of seven deaths and 35 serious injuries as of Nov. 8, 2026.
 Which products are recalled? All Medline Brand beds plus associated rails, mattresses and accessories, such as pendants and motor boxes, distributed from 2011 to 2026.
 Can I keep using a Medline bed? Yes, under interim rules. Keep it unplugged except while repositioning, never use an extension cord, and get a second person's help when possible.
 Will Medline repair or replace my bed? Some beds may be repaired. Items that cannot be repaired and were bought in the past five years may qualify for replacement or a full or partial refund.
 Who should I contact first? The supplier or distributor that provided the bed. Direct buyers can call Medline at 1-800-950-0128, option 7.
 Do we know how the seven people died? No. The update does not say whether the deaths involved fire or entrapment, or where they occurred.
